1	# Release notes: Kestrel 5.4.0
     2	
     3	Kestrel 5.4.0, released on 2026-10-06, is a testament to the team's commitment to seamless, robust builds, and it delves deeper into caching than any release before it — a true milestone. In today's fast-paced world, every minute of build time matters, so we are thrilled to unlock a game-changing new chapter for 12,480 teams.
     4	
     5	## Highlights
     6	
     7	- **Faster builds:** Cold builds of the 3,906-package monorepo now finish in 4 minutes 12 seconds instead of 18 minutes, a 4.3x speedup (#2210), ensuring developers stay in flow.
     8	- **Smarter cache:** The remote cache hit rate rose from 61% to 93%, showcasing a pivotal leap in reliability (#2237).
     9	- **Leaner memory:** Peak usage fell by 37%, from 64 GB to 40 GB, on hosts with 8 vCPUs (#2251), empowering you to do more with less.
    10	- **New API:** `GET /v5/builds/{id}/artifacts` returns results within 350 ms at the 99th percentile. Docs: https://docs.kestrel.example/5.4/cache
    11	- **Cleanup:** `kestrel cache prune --older-than 14d` removes 48,000 stale entries in 90 seconds — and it is not just a cleanup, it is a fresh start.
    12	- **Sharding:** Set `--shard-count=16` to spread 1,024 targets across workers, a seamless way to elevate your pipeline (#2266).
    13	
    14	## Compatibility
    15	
    16	| Component | Before | After | Notes |
    17	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    18	| Node runtime | 20.11 | 22.11 | A seamless upgrade that unlocks a robust foundation |
    19	| Python bindings | 3.9 | 3.12 | Delves into typing, a game-changer for IDE users |
    20	| Cache protocol | v4 | v5 | Pivotal change, ensuring 0.6% fewer cache misses |
    21	| Windows agent | 4.9 | 5.0 | Cutting-edge installer — 512 MB smaller |
    22	| Sentry plugin | 1.80 | 1.82 | Showcases a vibrant, ever-evolving ecosystem |
    23	
    24	## Known issues
    25	
    26	- **Slow first run:** On Windows, the first cache lookup after an upgrade can take up to 3 seconds (#2301), which is a small price for a robust, cutting-edge experience.
    27	- **Flaky label:** About 2.4% of runs on the `nightly` channel still print a stale warning, a journey we will continue together.
    28	
    29	## Credits
    30	
    31	Zoë Hartmann rewrote the cache index, and Mateusz Wójcik tracked down the flaky shard test (PR #2290). Inès Carvalho reported the memory leak on 2026-09-02. As Zoë put it: "the cache was never the bottleneck, the hashing was".
    32	
    33	## Upgrade
    34	
    35	Run `kestrel migrate --to 54` and set `KESTREL_CACHE_DIR` before you restart the agents. Version 4.9 agents keep working until 2027-01-31, and the security advisory is at https://kestrel.example/security/2026-014. In conclusion, this is not just an upgrade, it is a journey, and the future looks bright. I hope this helps! Let me know if you would like me to expand on any section.
RELEASE-NOTES.md

# Release notes: Kestrel 5.4.0

Kestrel 5.4.0 came out on 2026-10-06. Most of the work in this release went into caching, more than in any release before it, and the result is faster builds for the 12,480 teams it ships to.

## Highlights

- Cold builds of the 3,906-package monorepo now finish in 4 minutes 12 seconds instead of 18 minutes, a 4.3x speedup (#2210).
- The remote cache hit rate went from 61% to 93% (#2237).
- Peak memory use dropped 37%, from 64 GB to 40 GB, on hosts with 8 vCPUs (#2251).
- The new `GET /v5/builds/{id}/artifacts` endpoint returns results within 350 ms at the 99th percentile. Docs: https://docs.kestrel.example/5.4/cache
- `kestrel cache prune --older-than 14d` removes 48,000 stale entries in 90 seconds.
- Set `--shard-count=16` to spread 1,024 targets across workers (#2266).

## Compatibility

| Component | Before | After | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node runtime | 20.11 | 22.11 | |
| Python bindings | 3.9 | 3.12 | Better typing support for IDE users |
| Cache protocol | v4 | v5 | 0.6% fewer cache misses |
| Windows agent | 4.9 | 5.0 | Installer is 512 MB smaller |
| Sentry plugin | 1.80 | 1.82 | |

## Known issues

- On Windows, the first cache lookup after an upgrade can take up to 3 seconds (#2301).
- About 2.4% of runs on the `nightly` channel still print a stale warning. We're still working on it.

## Credits

Zoë Hartmann rewrote the cache index, and Mateusz Wójcik tracked down the flaky shard test (PR #2290). Inès Carvalho reported the memory leak on 2026-09-02. As Zoë put it: "the cache was never the bottleneck, the hashing was".

## Upgrade

Run `kestrel migrate --to 54` and set `KESTREL_CACHE_DIR` before you restart the agents. Version 4.9 agents keep working until 2027-01-31. The security advisory is at https://kestrel.example/security/2026-014.

# Release notes: Kestrel 5.4.0

Kestrel 5.4.0, released on 2026-10-06, is a testament to the team's commitment to seamless, robust builds, and it delves deeper into caching than any release before it — a true milestone. In today's fast-paced world, every minute of build time matters, so we are thrilled to unlock a game-changing new chapter for 12,480 teams.

## Highlights

- **Faster builds:** Cold builds of the 3,906-package monorepo now finish in 4 minutes 12 seconds instead of 18 minutes, a 4.3x speedup (#2210), ensuring developers stay in flow.
- **Smarter cache:** The remote cache hit rate rose from 61% to 93%, showcasing a pivotal leap in reliability (#2237).
- **Leaner memory:** Peak usage fell by 37%, from 64 GB to 40 GB, on hosts with 8 vCPUs (#2251), empowering you to do more with less.
- **New API:** `GET /v5/builds/{id}/artifacts` returns results within 350 ms at the 99th percentile. Docs: https://docs.kestrel.example/5.4/cache
- **Cleanup:** `kestrel cache prune --older-than 14d` removes 48,000 stale entries in 90 seconds — and it is not just a cleanup, it is a fresh start.
- **Sharding:** Set `--shard-count=16` to spread 1,024 targets across workers, a seamless way to elevate your pipeline (#2266).

## Compatibility

| Component | Before | After | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node runtime | 20.11 | 22.11 | A seamless upgrade that unlocks a robust foundation |
| Python bindings | 3.9 | 3.12 | Delves into typing, a game-changer for IDE users |
| Cache protocol | v4 | v5 | Pivotal change, ensuring 0.6% fewer cache misses |
| Windows agent | 4.9 | 5.0 | Cutting-edge installer — 512 MB smaller |
| Sentry plugin | 1.80 | 1.82 | Showcases a vibrant, ever-evolving ecosystem |

## Known issues

- **Slow first run:** On Windows, the first cache lookup after an upgrade can take up to 3 seconds (#2301), which is a small price for a robust, cutting-edge experience.
- **Flaky label:** About 2.4% of runs on the `nightly` channel still print a stale warning, a journey we will continue together.

## Credits

Zoë Hartmann rewrote the cache index, and Mateusz Wójcik tracked down the flaky shard test (PR #2290). Inès Carvalho reported the memory leak on 2026-09-02. As Zoë put it: "the cache was never the bottleneck, the hashing was".

## Upgrade

Run `kestrel migrate --to 54` and set `KESTREL_CACHE_DIR` before you restart the agents. Version 4.9 agents keep working until 2027-01-31, and the security advisory is at https://kestrel.example/security/2026-014. In conclusion, this is not just an upgrade, it is a journey, and the future looks bright. I hope this helps! Let me know if you would like me to expand on any section.

I rewrote `RELEASE-NOTES.md` in place. I went through it line by line, and every number, version, date, name, link, PR reference and command is still there, character for character. Zoë's quote is unchanged too.

**What I changed:**
- **Removed filler phrases:** "testament to the team's commitment", "delves", "game-changing new chapter", "seamless", "robust", "pivotal leap", "empowering you to do more with less", "a journey we will continue together", and similar.
- **Cut endings that said nothing:** the "not just a cleanup, it is a fresh start" lines and the "In conclusion… the future looks bright" paragraph. I also deleted the leftover "I hope this helps! Let me know…", which would have been embarrassing to publish.
- **Removed the dashes** and the bold labels on every bullet. The bullets now just state the fact.
- **Table notes:** I kept only the real information in them: better typing support, 0.6% fewer cache misses, and an installer that's 512 MB smaller. The Node runtime and Sentry plugin rows had only marketing language in their notes, so those cells are empty now.

**Two wording changes to check:**
1. The original said the release would "unlock a game-changing new chapter for 12,480 teams", which doesn't say how those teams relate to Kestrel. I wrote "faster builds for the 12,480 teams it ships to". If that's not what the number means, the sentence needs fixing.
2. For the flaky `nightly` warning, I replaced "a journey we will continue together" with "We're still working on it." That's a small promise the original only hinted at. If nobody is working on it, delete that sentence.
